| [CASE-053](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-053.md) v2 | Contextuality tests on human judgement data | The published tests of contextuality proper on elicited human judgements, read together. The null that meets every condition is the record's own [LIT-264](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-264.md): attitudinal and lexical data, none contextual under Contextuality-by-Default. Wang's thesis adds a Bell-type null on meaning judgements. The positive results miss a condition: Cervantes and Dzhafarov's "Snow Queen" is contextual with high reliability but its content is instructed attribute matching, and Lo, Sadrzadeh and Mansfield's Winograd schemas have the right content but a violation of about one standard deviation. No contextual pragmatic data are documented; "none in behavioural data" is too broad. | Active |
| [CASE-065](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-065.md) | Two satisfaction questions across a rendering | Haberstroh, Oyserman, Schwarz, Kühnen and Ji (2002), Experiment 2, asked German and Chinese students the same two satisfaction questions, in a back-translated Chinese version, in both orders. The part–whole correlation depends on order in the German administration and reverses in the Chinese one, and the authors explain it by a pragmatic mechanism. Only correlations are reported, so the case shows the bound's contrapositive in kind, not in number. Moore's Clinton–Gore poll, held through [LIT-834](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-834.md), supplies the number: an order effect of total variation about 0.095, against a sampling floor of about 0.03 per order at poll sizes, so 2ε is about as large as the effect it would certify. | Active |
| [CASE-068](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-068.md) | Risk messages passed down diffusion chains | In two serial-reproduction experiments on risk messages, each link's message was coded for content and, on a separate scheme, for the evaluative stance of its statements toward the hazard. Content got shorter, less accurate and more divergent; the evaluative signal survived and drifted negative, and re-exposure to the balanced source did not undo the drift. The transmitters' own risk perception, measured by questionnaire, predicts the direction of the change. Documented chain evidence for evaluative stance; none for footing. | Active |
| [CASE-070](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-070.md) v2 | BLEU-tied systems differing on ты and вы | Two English-to-Russian subtitle translation systems score the same BLEU (32.40 and 32.38, not significantly different). A documented instance, on a pragmatic distinction, of two realizations equal under a standard probe family and different under an independently built one. An ML paper that neither record holds. | Active |

| [CASE-207](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-207.md) v2 | The square twist | Filed at the owner's request on 2026-11-05, to file "one or more CASEs for origami as a toy model of a resource bounded constraint configuration space". Silverberg et al. 2015 ([NOTE-1554](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1554.md)): the square twist's crease pattern is isostatic, and rigidly it has only two isolated states, unfolded and folded, yet it folds by bending its facets, a hidden degree of freedom with its own energy scale. The authors' thesis is that the number of degrees of freedom changes with the energy scale probed; their kinematic skeleton, with bending capped at 10°, has a critical plane angle near 23° separating a connected configuration space from a disconnected one. Read as a resource model, the configuration space is indexed by the budget rather than fixed, and widening the admissible moves is itself priced, which joins the vertex under a budget ([CASE-206](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-206.md)) to the curved vertex whose moves no budget widens ([CASE-204](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-204.md)). A mechanical study; its organizational reading is an analogy. Adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CASE-208](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-208.md) | A prestressed Kresling stack | Filed at the owner's request on 2026-11-05, to file "one or more CASEs for origami as a toy model of a resource bounded constraint configuration space". Zang, Zhao, Misseroni and Paulino ([NOTE-1569](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1569.md)): a stack of three bistable Kresling cells has 8 stable states and 56 ordered transitions; 32 are feasible, 16 cannot be made without passing through other stable states, and 8 are blocked by the order of the cells' energy barriers. Springs and handles, applied from outside, prestress the cells and reorder the barriers in place, which makes the 8 blocked transitions feasible; the 16 are not opened. Read as a resource model, the barriers bound the transitions, and the blocked ones are opened by changing the architecture, not by a larger load: the physical counterpart of [CASE-198](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-198.md). Jules et al. ([NOTE-1617](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1617.md)) show the same dependence on the order of thresholds in a Kresling memory. A mechanical study; its organizational reading is an analogy. Adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |

| [CASE-387](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-387.md) | Satellite clock comparison checked by fibre | From Riedel et al. (2020): four European institutes compare their clocks for 26 days through local masers and two satellite links at once, TWSTFT (signal exchange over a geostationary satellite) and GPS PPP. Each link estimates the frequency difference of each remote clock pair. The two estimates agree within their uncertainties, and for LNE-SYRTE and PTB both agree with an optical-fibre comparison of the same clocks, one run at the same time. A measured correspondence between remote local standards is checked against evidence that the measurement producing it did not produce: [CLAIM-510](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-510.md)'s own clock example, in practice.
